title: Strict tower complex functor and universal K-injective derived model
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories, allowing independent object and morphism universes. Their unbounded derived categories $D(\mathcal A),D(\mathcal B)$ are localizations of integer cochain complexes at quasi-isomorphisms, with localization functors $Q_{\mathcal A},Q_{\mathcal B}$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], in a chosen common localization universe. For an additive functor $G:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor], define $\operatorname{tower}(G):C(\mathbf N^{op}\!\to\mathcal A)\to C(\mathbf N^{op}\!\to\mathcal B)$ by applying $G$ at every tower level and every cochain degree, to transitions, differentials and chain maps. Level $n\in\mathbf N$ represents positive level $n+1$. For any functor $H:C(\mathcal A)\to C(\mathcal B)$, a derived model consists of a functor $R:D(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal B)$ and a natural transformation $\eta:H Q_{\mathcal B}\to Q_{\mathcal A}R$ exhibiting $R$ as the total right derived functor: every natural transformation $H Q_{\mathcal B}\to Q_{\mathcal A}T$, for $T:D(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal B)$, factors uniquely through $\eta$ by a natural transformation $R\to T$. In addition, $\eta_I$ is an isomorphism for every K-injective complex $I$, where K-injective means every chain map from an acyclic complex to $I$ is null-homotopic. This defines the data of a model and asserts no existence of such a model.
